lines: Who is affected?
The dMAT requirement applies to Indian Master’s applicants whose undergraduate degree falls under any of the following disciplines:
• Engineering / Technology:
• All degrees titled B.Tech or B.Eng regardless of specialization.
• All other undergraduate degrees in Engineering regardless of degree nomenclature (e.g., BS Research, B.Voc, or B.Sc. in Engineering tracks).
• Commerce & Economics: All undergraduate degrees in Commerce, Accounting, Finance, or Economics.
• Business & Management: All undergraduate degrees in Business Administration or Management Studies.
• Tourism, Travel & Hospitality: All undergraduate degrees in Tourism, Travel, Hotel, and Hospitality Management.

• Integrated & Dual-Degree Programs: Applicants completing integrated Bachelor-Master or dual-degree programs must take the dMAT if any component or major field of their program falls within one of the affected disciplines listed above.

For applicants in these fields, the dMAT is a required part of the APS documentation for applications relating to intakes from the summer semester 2027 onwards, unless a transitional exemption applies.
Applicants who have already completed the APS procedure and have received their APS certificate are not required to take the dMAT for that completed APS procedure.

Applicants who completed their APS online registration on or after 29 June 2026 and shipped their APS application documents on or after 29 June 2026 are required to submit a dMAT certificate, provided that their previous degree falls within one of the affected fields and their application relates to the Summer Semester 2027 Master intake or a later Master intake. How is the dMAT structured?
The dMAT consists of two modules: a core module and a subject module (General Academic Module) .
The core module measures general cognitive and analytical skills. It consists of three subtests.

The subject module tests the ability to apply these cognitive and analytical skills to academic problem solving in a general academic module. The tasks consist of a combination of a typical problem and related questions. The dMAT therefore requires developed transfer and application skills rather than memorised factual knowledge.
Will I automatically be denied an APS certificate if I submit a low dMAT score?
No. The dMAT is not a stand-alone pass/fail test for the APS certificate.

APS India verifies the authenticity and formal plausibility of academic documents. The dMAT certificate provides a required additional academic test result issued by g.a.s.t. and forms part of the APS documentation for the affected applicant groups.

A low dMAT score does not automatically lead to a refusal of the APS certificate. The APS certificate will document the APS verification result and, where applicable, reflect the dMAT result as part of the applicant’s APS documentation.

How much does the dMAT cost?
The dMAT test fee is charged by g.a.s.t. The current fee is €150.00 and is payable during registration. Payment details will be shown on the dMAT website during registration.
